_comment: Constraint budget, checked by scripts/check-budget.mjs (`just budget`).
`constraints` is the exact snarkjs r1cs count and must be updated in the
same commit as any circuit change, so the change lands as a reviewable diff.
`domain` is the Groth16 FFT domain the circuit must fit; exceeding it means
a larger ptau and roughly double the proving time.
2x2 and 3x3 fit 2^16. Transact(10,3,3) clears it by 13 constraints, so a
change worth 3 constraints in one of its 6 per-slot gadgets costs the
domain. Transact(10,4,4) does not fit 2^16 at all and is budgeted against
4x6 and tree_update_batch are the depth-11 pair and both sit in 2^17.
tree_update_batch is the tighter of the two at ~17.5k of headroom against
4x6's ~30.7k, because it grew on both axes at once: four more leaf slots
at roughly 12k each, plus the depth level across all eight. It, not the
transact circuit, is what a further widening would break first.
2x2, 3x3 and 4x4 are still depth 10 and cannot share a tree with the
depth-11 pair; they are kept compiling, not kept usable.
